sentences.text: Some feathers of Archaeornithura feature a central groove, a trait associated with derived flight feathers.
The thighbone of Archaeornithura is short relative to the length of the tarsometatarsus.
Archaeornithura meemannae is the oldest known member of the ornithuromorph lineage, which includes all modern birds and their extinct relatives.
Archaeornithura appears to have been adept at flying.
Two fossil specimens of Archaeornithura were found in the Huajiying Formation in Hebei Province, China.
Archaeornithura is the first ornithuromorph fossil discovered in the Huajiying Formation.
The species was named and described by an international team led by Wang and Zhou Zhonge from the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing.
The discovery of Archaeornithura was announced in the journal Nature Communications in May 2015.
Researchers Zhou and Wang hypothesize that these avian traits may have helped ornithuromorphs survive the Cretaceous-Paleogene mass extinction.
Archaeornithura is classified within the family Hongshanornithidae.
Phylogenetic analysis identified Archaeornithura as the sister taxon of Tianyuornis.
Archaeornithura lived during the Hauterivian age approximately 130.7 million years ago.
The time range for Archaeornithura is estimated from 132.6 to 125.77 million years ago.
